title: AI Chatbots Are Sending Shoppers to Fake Stores
dek: A Podqi study found risky shop links in ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity answers.

facts.label: Chatbot answers analyzed in the study
Brands tested, from Lululemon to Stüssy

caption:
Asked an AI where to buy your favorite brand? It might have sent you to a fake store. 🛑

A new study by anti-counterfeit firm Podqi tested ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity with shopping questions about 151 brands. Across 6,795 answers, the chatbots surfaced fake stores, knockoff sellers and hijacked or dead domains. Perplexity did worst at 15%, ChatGPT landed at 8%, and Gemini was lowest at 4%. In one case, Perplexity called a wrong page Stüssy's official store.

Smaller brands and regional store links were the biggest weak spots, and the timing matters: holiday shoppers are leaning on AI to find deals at stores they've never used. We're tracking this one closely at AI Parabellum.

The takeaway: treat AI store links as a starting point. Type the brand's address yourself, watch for too-good prices and odd domains, and pay with buyer protection.

Gemini 4%, ChatGPT 8%, Perplexity 15%. That's how often each chatbot showed risky shopping sites in Podqi's new study of 151 brands.

Before you check out this holiday season, verify the store yourself. A confident AI answer is not proof a site is real. 🔍
